title: Sum Without Plus
statement:
Add two 32-bit integers using only bitwise operations, shifts, and comparisons.

Contract
- `a` and `b` may be any `int`, positive, negative, or zero.
- Return `a + b` with Java `int` semantics: when the true sum does not fit in 32 bits, the
  result wraps around in two's complement, exactly as `a + b` would.
- Do not use `+`, `-`, `++`, `--`, or `Math.addExact`-style helpers in your solution. The tests
  cannot enforce this, so treat it as part of the exercise.

Examples
- `add(13, 29)` returns `42`.
- `add(-5, 3)` returns `-2`.
- `add(7, -7)` returns `0`.
hints: Add two single bits by hand: the sum bit is their XOR and the carry bit is their AND.
Do the same for whole words: XOR gives the sum ignoring carries, and AND shifted left by one gives the carries. Repeat until nothing is left to carry.

Loop while the carry word is non-zero; two's complement makes negatives and overflow work with no special cases. Intended complexity: O(1) per addition (at most 32 rounds) and O(1) space, so a batch of n additions costs O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
inputSyntax: Input: two integers separated by a space, for example: 13 29
